A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NLC adaptive backbone ensembling work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments comparing nine CLIP backbones, NLC ensembles, few-shot adaptations and robustness across classification benchmarks.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original diversity analyses, SuperLearner comparisons, seed variability reporting and image-text retrieval results.

M1.justification: NLC still predicts input-dependent backbone temperatures from concatenated visual features and combines logits, training with cross-entropy. Cascade and Tip-Adapter integrations already appear in v1. The explicit weighted-sum wording in v2 clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval on Flickr30k and MSCOCO, substantially extending coverage beyond classification. These experiments evaluate individual backbones and oracle combinations, not trained NLC retrieval. The original classification datasets and ImageNet distribution shifts remain.

E2.justification: SuperLearner is added to the zero-shot and linear-classifier comparisons in Tables C.1/D.2 and the Tip-Adapter comparisons in Tables F.3–F.6. GAC remains evaluated; its description moves to Appendix C. Figure J.3 also includes classical ensemble comparators in the accuracy-versus-compute comparison.

E3.justification: Section 2.2 introduces a controlled comparison of backbone architecture, pretraining source and checkpoints at epochs 31/32. Retrieval adds Recall@1/5/10 evaluation, and Table G.1 extends training samples from 16 to 32 per class. The stated diversity metric also changes from a specific backbone's correct predictions to the intersection across all backbones.

E4.justification: New Section 2.2, Figure 6 and Tables I.1–I.2 investigate whether complementarity comes from architecture, pretraining data or neighboring checkpoints. Appendix J expands efficiency comparisons, and Appendix G extends sample-count sensitivity to 32 shots. Earlier perturbation, distribution-shift, temperature and backbone-combination analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G first reports training with five seeds and summarizes mean performance standard deviations of 0.62 for one shot and 0.48 for 32 shots. v1 provides no corresponding seed-count or performance-variability reporting. This establishes new reporting, not an increase from a documented earlier run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds SuperLearner scores, diversity/oracle results, 32-shot results and retrieval recalls. SuperLearner matches NLC's reported 1.6-point mean linear-classifier improvement in Table D.2. Table B.1 revises GFLOPs, including RN50 from 34.0 to 18.2 and ViT-L-14-336 from 858.0 to 395.2. Appendix C corrects prose gains from 35.1 to 39.1 and 8.1 to 9.3; most existing NLC accuracy entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: As written, footnote 1 changes diversity from one minus a specific backbone's correct-count divided by the union count to one minus the all-backbone intersection divided by the union. Section 2.2 explains this revised definition and its boundary cases. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the central claims of backbone complementarity, input-adaptive temperature ensembling, few-shot effectiveness and computational efficiency, including the headline 39.1% and 9.1% improvements. The additional comparisons principally provide evidence and positioning for these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the strongest complementarity to architecture rather than pretraining data or nearby training checkpoints, while acknowledging the absence of initialization-only controls. It interprets the seed results as stability under sample variation. Limitations now acknowledge retrieval oracle evidence and discuss distillation and retraining instead of the earlier unexplored early-fusion alternative.

D1.justification: Section 3 identifies NLC fitting data as a holdout from each target training set, and Appendix F explicitly identifies ImageNet as the dataset behind the retained few-shot summary tables. These refine documentation without establishing changed experiments. Appendix A's optimizer, learning rate, hidden width, hardware, cascade threshold and model-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 identifies SuperLearner as the closest ensemble framework and emphasizes input-conditioned temperatures as the distinction. It adds related work by Roth, Ramé and Zhong on model complementarity and by Varshney and Baral on cascading. The broader related-work coverage remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, related work and limitations receive targeted edits. v2 inserts a diversity subsection and new appendices, while retaining and renumbering the original overlap and combination appendices. Citation style, author details and publication headers change, and acknowledgements replace the generic societal-impact paragraph; most prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the diversity boxplot in Figure 6, Tables I.1–I.2, retrieval Table K.3 and the expanded efficiency plot in Figure J.3. Ensemble comparison plots and several tables incorporate new comparator or sample-count rows. Conference formatting also changes the layout. Existing temperature and overlap graphics are retained rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The SuperLearner comparisons, diversity controls and five-seed summary strengthen empirical support, while revised compute values improve consistency with Figure 3. The gains are limited by aggregate uncertainty reporting and an overstated new retrieval summary: Table K.3 gives a Flickr30k text-retrieval R@1 gap of 10.5 points (98.8 versus 88.3), although the prose claims 20 points.
